recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-22651 unless Pharmacy later chooses to revisit the broader MedicationStatement effective[x] narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-22651 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked that MedicationUsage/MedicationStatement.effective[x] not imply that active medication use must always omit effectivePeriod.end; the approved wording omits the end only for indefinite ongoing use and includes a known end date.
initial_application: The Jira snapshot records a 2019-06-18 committed-and-merged implementation link. In the local branch ancestry, commit 634360b51d40494b5427df25cc2ecce831d928e4 is the visible GF 22651 application, changing the then-current MedicationUsage spreadsheet effective[x] comment from the unconditional omitted-end sentence to the indefinite-use/known-end-date distinction.
additional_context: MedicationStatement is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current source has moved from the older MedicationUsage spreadsheet representation to structuredefinition-MedicationStatement.xml plus mapping exception sources. The originating Zulip thread supports the Jira rationale, and Confluence reference search found no separate conflicting minutes.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/medicationstatement/structuredefinition-MedicationStatement.xml already states that effectivePeriod.end is omitted only when ongoing use is expected to continue indefinitely and included when known; the Event mapping exception source repeats the same resource-specific wording.
